I will keep to the cropping pattern I trust most here in Quzhou County: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same land. I know this system, it matches our climate on the North China Plain, and it spreads my risk better than switching to something unfamiliar. I am 58, my schooling is limited, so I would rather do the work I understand well and can manage steadily than chase a complicated crop. At the start of the season, my main job is to manage the wheat already in the field with topdressing, irrigation, and disease control, then after wheat harvest I will sow summer maize quickly to catch moisture and heat. I will use improved or hybrid seed, not old saved seed, because I want stable yield and cleaner field performance. I will not overdo fertilizer, but I will feed enough nitrogen for yield and add phosphorus and potassium so the crop does not go weak. I will irrigate wheat more than maize because wheat here depends more on timely water, especially around jointing and grain filling. I will use rotary tillage for wheat establishment because it is familiar and reliable for me, and I will use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest because it saves time and helps me sow fast in the tight rotation window.
